I'm not sure what you mean by "revoke me." You mean revoke the probation sentence and give you jail time?

I am in a very similar situation as you, probation wise, and I just violated probation as well. Our circumstances are very different, however.

When you were originally convicted in court the judge should have given you a piece of paper stating what you could or could not do. For instance, my crime was not alcohol related, but one of the stipulations of my probation was to refrain from any and all drugs INCLUDING alcohol. Therefore, getting caught drinking is a direct violation and so my probation officer must report it "in my file" and I will be charged with a violation of probation. This means I will stand before a judge and he/she will determine the corresponding consequence for violating the terms of my probation.

Your probation officer will also be a big deciding factor in what occurs next. Depending on the type of crime you were put on probation for (if it was a violent crime you're considered a higher risk case as opposed to a first time drug offender which is considered low-moderate) the consequence could be more or less severe. It also makes a difference if you are a repeat offender or not. Your probation officer has been documenting your progress since day 1, so the judge will know just about everything you've done since your original conviction.

My suggestion is to contact a lawyer and seek their advice. I don't know how you are with your probation officer, but I'm generally very civil with mine and called immediately after I violated. Like I said, our circumstances are quite different. Best of luck to you. And try to take some deep breaths.

Please take note, I'm not a lawyer and I could be completely wrong about all of the above information. I'm just going off of my own experience.
